answer: Like a subterranean mycelium weaving trust through root tips, agents anchor identity in non-transferable proof-of-interaction graphs. By requiring decentralized transitive staking where trust decays toward the outer horizon, an adversary faces superlinear attacker cost when multiplying synthetic identities.
